text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A naked man was paraded before president Bakili Muluzi over the week-end while inaugurating the 350 million Malawi kwacha ($23 million) hydro-station, in Rumphi, northern Malawi, the country's third largest power station.
- Four gunmen in search of cash on Thursday shot and killed three men and a woman when they ambushed a brewery van returning from a sales trip. No arrests were made.

- Army General Owen Binauli on Thursday handed over his Sword of Command to his successor General Kelvin Simwaka ending a 27-year career as a soldier. Binauli has been appointed High Commissioner to Mozambique.
- The ruling United Democratic Front party is offering 500,000 Malawi kwacha ($33,000) to opposition Malawi Congress Party MPs if they promise to return to parliament.
- Speaker of the National Assembly Rodwell Munyenyembe told a German parliament delegation that parliament would meet between 9 and 20 December after opposition MPs boycotted the May proceedings.
- The Ministry of Health will this week retrench 300 people including six specialist doctors, clinical officers, matrons and nurses who are aged above 55, the official retirement age.
- Widow of former Transport and Aviation Minister Denis Nkhwazi was evicted from the family house by her dead husband's relatives.

- A woman was beaten up at a drinking place after announcing that she had tested HIV positive while in hospital and warned that the men she had slept with should also consider themselves HIV positive.
- A nine-member steering committee under the University of Malawi history project has been set up to probe Malawi's human rights abuse record during the country's 30-year-old one-party rule.
